doc.title: A.B. Spellman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 19, 2022

title: Why he cannot write poetry to jazz
summary: Jazz and poetry are different; he writes to classical music, not jazz, and reflects on Bach as an improviser.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: What part did your love of jazz play in the construction of your poems?

It’s a difficult question to answer straight on. The thing is that they are entirely different things. Jazz, as stimulus, jazz has a way of keeping that part of the mind that hooks up the, hooks up reason and intuition which basically is what poetry is. They could work that way as jazz as an accompanist. But on the other hand I can’t write to jazz you know. I cannot. I cannot write a word to jazz. I can write to classical music you know but I cannot write to jazz. Charlie Parker, John Coltrane, I can’t write a word.

I just noticed that struck me, because I was reading “Dear John Coltrane” your poem, and it says, “In the dead of night I’m writing poetry in another hotel room and J.S. Bach is on the radio.” And I went back and read that again, because the title, “John Coltrane,” and you’re listening to J.S. Bach. It was a nice juxtaposition.

Yeah, yeah. I mean it’s all music. It’s all music. It wouldn’t surprise me if Bach were alive today that he’d be a jazz musician. He was a great improviser after all and I think probably that may be how he did most of his compositions. For a man to write that many cantatas can’t possibly have been sitting there putting it all down. I think he improvised a lot of music and had people copied it for him as he played. That was a guess I got from a composer of my acquaintance. But at any rate, yeah, I think that there is again that kind of note to note discovery that you hear in the great musicians, you know where you know that they are finding something every time they write or play a phrase. That is an element of the music that I think is what makes it, which distinguishes the quality of musicians. There is always something new to them and to us in everything they write.
